newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm, unable to pierce resistance.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm, unable to pierce resistance.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted selective gains on Tuesday as activity enlivened on minor cash influx, but trade remained range-bound, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 finished up 737.58 points at 63,642.41 after easing from the midday close of 63,788. Daily volume nearly doubled to 6.12 trillion lira ($69.1 million) from Monday's 3.4 trillion ($38.6 million).
"There was minor profit-taking in the afternoon, as was expected after the morning selective buys. Cash entry is still insufficient," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank.
Reaction buys, mainly in shares of largely state owned stocks had emerged this morning after support of the index was confirmed at around 62,500 yesterday.
Brokers said the index was likely to continue drifting in narrow ranges unless cash entry increased.
